dublinCore.description: Interactive simulation of a double-buffered real-time FIR filter. An animated pipeline shows the input buffer filling, the processor filtering the previous block and the output buffer playing the block before that; a time line checks each block's busy time (overhead, filter work and random background bursts) against the deadline T = B/fs, and a load chart and meter show per-block and average processor load with underruns in red. Read-outs give latency 2B/fs, the MAC rate fs*L, processor capacity, expected and counted underruns, and the quantization noise floor of the word length. Processor figures are typical, illustrative values.
relation: Chapter 15: Signal Processing Applications and AI Integration

searchKeywords: fixed-point noise floor 6.02 dB per bit

learningObjectives: Calculate the block period T = B/fs and the buffering latency 2B/fs for a given sample rate and block size
Calculate the MAC rate fs*L of an FIR filter and the processor load it produces for a given clock rate and MACs per cycle
Explain why a processor with an average load below 100 % can still miss deadlines, and how the block size changes the miss rate
Compare fixed-point and floating-point word lengths by their noise floor (about -6.02 B dBFS) and their computational cost
Evaluate a combination of processor, word length and block size against latency, load-margin and noise-floor requirements
prerequisites: FIR filters and the convolution sum
Basic quantization in bits and decibels

misconceptions.misconception: If the average load is below 100 %, the system meets real-time deadlines
misconceptions.correction: Deadlines are judged block by block; random background work makes some blocks exceed the block period even when the average is well below 100 %
misconceptions.evidence: The default settings show an average load of 70.7 % with expected misses of 5.1 % and red bars in the load chart

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger buffer always cures dropouts
misconceptions.correction: Larger blocks smooth short-term variation and always add latency; when the average load exceeds 100 % they make misses more frequent
misconceptions.evidence: With 256 taps on the MCU (average load 109.1 %) the expected misses rise from 76.2 % at B = 32 to 96.9 % at B = 512

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Real-time block processing simulator. A pipeline shows the input buffer filling, the processor filtering the previous block and the output buffer playing the block before that. A time line shows whether the filter, the per-block overhead and random background bursts finish before the deadline T = B/fs, and a bar chart shows the processor load of the last 60 blocks with missed deadlines in red. Selects set the sample rate, processor, word length and animation speed; sliders set the block size, filter taps and background load.

controls.label: Processor
controls.description: Chooses a processor preset (typical, illustrative clock rate, MACs per cycle and per-block overhead)

controls.label: Word length
controls.description: Chooses 16-bit fixed, 24-bit fixed or 32-bit float arithmetic; changes MACs per cycle and the noise floor

controls.label: Speed
controls.description: Animation rate in blocks per second (the simulated timing is unaffected)

controls.label: Block size B
controls.description: Sets the block size as a power of two, B = 2^value samples (16 to 4096)

controls.label: Filter taps L
controls.description: Sets the number of FIR filter taps (multiply-accumulates per output sample)

controls.label: Background load
controls.description: Average share of the processor taken by other tasks, arriving as random 50 microsecond bursts (no effect on the FPGA)

controls.label: Run / Pause
controls.description: Starts, pauses and resumes the animation (it opens paused)

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Restores the default settings and restarts the simulation

visualElements.description: Pipeline of input buffer (block k+1 filling), processor (block k) and output buffer (block k-1 playing, red on underrun)
Processor time line for one block: overhead, filter work and background bursts against the deadline T = B/fs
Bar chart of processor load per block for the last 60 blocks with the 100 % deadline, the 80 % margin line and missed blocks outlined in red, plus an average-load meter
Read-outs of block period, latency, noise floor, MAC rate, capacity, filter and overhead load, average load, expected misses and counted underruns

model.description: Each block's busy time is the FIR work B*L/(clock*MACs per cycle) plus a fixed per-block overhead plus N background bursts of 50 microseconds, with N Poisson-distributed with mean b*T/50 us. A block misses its deadline (output underrun) when the busy time exceeds the block period T = B/fs. Processor parameters are typical, illustrative values.
equations: t_busy = B L / capacity + overhead / f_clk + N * 50 us, N ~ Poisson(b T / 50 us)
algorithms: Inverse-CDF Poisson sampling with a seeded PRNG
Poisson tail probability summed in the log domain
limitations: Processor figures are illustrative, not data-sheet values
A late block is counted as one underrun and the next block starts on time (no cascading)
Only direct-form FIR filtering is modelled

instructionalStrategies: Predict the block period, MAC rate and load before reading them
Table of expected misses and latency against block size
Compare processors and word lengths against a design requirement
extensions: Add FFT-based fast convolution as an alternative algorithm and compare its cost per block
Add a priority-scheduling option for background tasks
